page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with 8 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 31.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.88 GB per core. It includes a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance division between CPU-bound and GPU-bound operations. The Intel Xeon CPU delivers weak performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, placing in the bottom 25% for both single-core and multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth is average for large uncached blocks but weak for cached small blocks. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance in machine learning tasks. LLM inference benchmarks for a medium 7B model show top-tier prompt processing speeds in the top 10% and strong text generation speeds in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance serves as an entry-level GPU platform. It avoids the high costs associated with premium accelerators, making it a viable option for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not demand massive CPU compute power. Due to the weak CPU and database benchmark results, it is not recommended for heavy general-purpose computing, high-throughput web serving, or database operations. Instead, the hardware configuration is best suited for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, and GPU-assisted video or image processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 vCPUs, 31.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture via the KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local storage and provides a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While CPU and memory benchmarks are generally weak, placing in the bottom 25% for standard compute tasks, the NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers top-tier performance for LLM prompt processing and strong text generation speeds on medium-sized models. This hardware profile offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads, making it highly suitable for machine learning inference, small to medium LLM deployment, and lightweight CUDA tasks, while remaining less optimal for CPU-intensive or database-heavy operations.
